name: Horse Feed
description:
A ten-pound ration of dry grain and chopped fodder, measured out for a working mount. It is sold loose or in a light paper wrap; a durable sack or feed bag is a separate purchase.

The daily ration follows the 2014 equipment baseline. The GM determines adjustments for the animal, grazing and workload. Drinking water is not included. Use 'Feed one daily ration' when the entire portion is given to an animal; this consumes one sale unit and provides no healing.
saleUnit: One day's ten-pound ration of dry animal feed

weight.notes: Ten pounds is deliberately retained for the full daily feed ration so pack-animal provisioning remains meaningful; a reusable bag is not included.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: 2014 SRD 5.1 equipment: animal feed is priced by the day and listed at 10 lb; this project changes its price. Original wording; project prices and adjusted weights. See docs/GENERAL_STORE_REVIEW.md.

use.name: Feed one daily ration
use.condition: Use when one complete ten-pound feed ration is given to an animal. Water is separate.

name: Feed Bag
description:
A stout canvas bag with a broad hanging strap, shaped to hold feed within easy reach of a tethered horse or similar mount. Its seams and mouth are reinforced for repeated use.

Sold empty. It holds up to 10 lb or half a cubic foot of dry feed, whichever limit is reached first. Feed is bought separately and adds its own weight. The bag is not watertight; fit and supervise it appropriately for the animal.

weight.notes: Half a pound for the empty canvas bag and strap; feed carried inside is counted separately.

name: Brush
description:
A small wooden-backed brush with stiff bristles and a cloth hand loop. It lifts loose dust and hair from a mount's coat during routine grooming.

One brush is supplied. It is an ordinary care tool, with no automatic Animal Handling bonus or effect on wounds and illness.

weight.notes: One tenth of a pound for the small wooden back, bristles and hand loop.

name: Curry Comb
description:
A hand-sized metal comb with rounded, toothed ridges and a short handle. Used carefully during grooming, it loosens dried mud and shedding hair from a mount's coat.

The comb is separate from a finishing brush. It grants no skill bonus and is not equipment for treating an injured animal.

weight.notes: One fifth of a pound for a light metal comb and short handle.

name: Horseshoes
description:
Four plain iron horseshoes with a small packet of fitting nails, supplied as an uninstalled set. They are ordinary farrier's stock for a suitably sized horse.

The listed price and weight cover the whole set. Skilled fitting, removal of old shoes and any reshaping are separate services. These mundane shoes provide no magical movement benefit or automatic speed increase.
saleUnit: One set of four iron horseshoes with fitting nails

weight.notes: Two pounds for four light ordinary shoes and their nails; size-specific heavy shoes may differ by GM ruling.

name: Tack Repair Kit
description:
A small roll containing an awl, heavy needle, waxed thread, leather patches, spare laces and two plain buckles. It supports minor repairs to sound straps, harnesses and saddlebags.

The purchase includes the roll and all listed supplies. It is not a full set of leatherworker's tools and grants no proficiency. Major damage or a failed load-bearing strap may need a craftsperson and replacement parts.

weight.notes: Three quarters of a pound for the complete compact tool roll and repair materials.

name: Halter
description:
An adjustable leather headcollar gives a handler a place to attach a lead rope on a horse or mule. Plain buckles allow a sensible fit around the animal's head.

The lead rope is separate. A halter contains no bit and is not a riding bridle; fitting it does not tame an animal or replace handling checks.
saleUnit: One adjustable leather halter for a horse or mule

weight.notes: Three quarters of a pound for the leather straps, buckles and attachment ring.

name: Lead Rope
description:
A ten-foot hemp lead has a reinforced loop for fastening to a suitable halter. Its short length lets a handler guide a standing or walking pack animal without carrying a full climbing coil.

The halter is separate. This working lead is not a certified climbing rope, and attaching it grants no automatic control of a frightened animal.
saleUnit: One ten-foot hemp lead with attachment loop

weight.notes: Three quarters of a pound for the short lead, reinforced loop and binding.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Saddle Blanket
description:
A dense wool pad lies beneath a properly fitted saddle to cushion pressure and take up sweat. Its broad rectangular shape can be folded to suit ordinary horse or mule tack.

The saddle and girth are separate. Padding cannot correct an unsuitable saddle or make an overloaded animal able to carry more.
saleUnit: One thick saddle pad for a horse or mule

weight.notes: Two and a half pounds for the thick wool pad, without saddle or fastening straps.

name: Horse Hobbles
description:
Two broad padded leather loops are joined by a short link to limit the stride of a trained resting horse. They are used with supervision and a suitable place for the animal to stand or graze.

They are not combat restraints and do not automatically restrain a creature. The GM resolves fitting, resistance and any risk to an unsuitable or frightened animal.
saleUnit: One pair of padded leather hobbles

weight.notes: Four tenths of a pound for the padded straps and short joining link.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Picket Line
description:
A stout thirty-foot line and two driven stakes establish a temporary tethering point in suitable ground. Individual animal leads attach separately along the line with enough spacing to avoid tangling.

Leads, halters and a hammer are separate. The purchase offers no fixed animal capacity or automatic restraint; soil, anchoring and behaviour determine safe use.
saleUnit: One thirty-foot hemp line with two iron stakes

weight.notes: Four pounds for the full line and both stakes; separate leads are excluded.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Saddlebags
description:
Two lidded leather bags are joined by a broad strap to hang on opposite sides of a suitable saddle. They are sold and weighed as one matched pair.

Balance the contents and count their weight against the mount's carried load. The pair holds up to 20 pounds within one cubic foot in total; the saddle and contents are separate.
saleUnit: One empty matched pair of leather saddlebags

weight.notes: Three pounds for the empty joined pair, including straps and closures.
